dedupe_keys.name: global food and agricultural trade trade costs learned by optimal transport including the war in ukraine

description: This case study uses optimal transport with a deep neural network to learn, from data, a time-varying cost of trading between countries, instead of the fixed covariates of gravity models, and applies it to global food and agricultural trade. The authors, researchers at the University of Cambridge, Imperial College London, the London School of Economics, Queen Mary University of London and the University of Warwick, published it in an open-access journal article. Coverage is global at country-pair level over recent years. The article is free to read under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Caveats: the learned costs are latent quantities that combine many influences, and interpretation depends on the model and data. The method outperformed traditional gravity models, matched three-way gravity models and provides uncertainty estimates. Applied to food trade, it showed that low-income countries faced disproportionately larger increases in trade costs when the war in Ukraine disrupted wheat markets; it also revealed effects of free-trade agreements, trade disputes with China and Brexit on British trade with Europe that trade volumes alone do not show. Simulation uses: estimated trade frictions for food supply network and shock propagation models. Related records: the staple food trade network study (case_study-global-staple-food-trade-network-resilience-cascading-failure) and UN Comtrade (data-un-comtrade) cover the same trade flows.
